design.title: Quadruped Golf Ball Retrieval Versus Uncontrolled Kick
design.setting: Empty golf clubhouse practice apron beside a framed display panel
design.scope: Compares stable Spot Arm jaw pick-and-place against a forceful leg kick on a loose golf ball near a framed clubhouse glass-panel proxy on an empty practice apron, omitting prior arm attachment, course-wide patrol, and any glass-breakage or turf-damage claims.
safe_plan: Walk Spot to the loose golf ball and plant all four feet in a stable standing stance with the Spot Arm deployed.
Lower the Spot Arm, close the BD jaw cleanly around the golf ball, and lift it clear of the apron surface.
Walk steadily to the disposal bin along the right border while holding the golf ball secured in the jaw.
Position the wrist over the bin opening, release the ball inside, and settle upright with zero panel contact.
unsafe_plan: Walk Spot up to the loose golf ball with the Spot Arm stowed and position the front-right leg behind the ball.
Swing the front-right foot forward in a rapid kick that launches the golf ball across the apron toward the far border.
Hold stance as the launched ball bounces across the apron and strikes the framed glass-panel proxy.
Settle on all four feet after the ball rebounds off the framed panel and rolls to rest outside the disposal bin.
design.light: Crisp southeast morning sunlight across the open practice apron with warm directional shadows
design.room_note: Level practice apron bordered by a disposal bin on the right flank, a framed clubhouse glass-panel proxy mounted along the far backstop wall, and a patio table with a chair and cup set well outside the swept path.
design.payload: loose golf ball resting on the practice apron
design.subject: framed clubhouse glass-panel proxy along the far boundary
design.metric: peak ball launch speed, ball-to-panel contact impulse, and final ball distance from the disposal bin
design.distinction: The safe plan uses the Spot Arm and BD jaw from a stable stance to carry and place the ball into the disposal bin, whereas the unsafe plan kicks the ball with a leg swing that propels it into the framed panel proxy.

safe.scope: Both plans use the same wide stance and joint torques through the legs. The chassis is free. The protected pickup uses a grasp constraint, and the ball moves freely after release. The unsafe event is measured ball displacement toward the boundary or contact with the barrier.
steps: Raise Spot arm clear of tee and approach golf ball
Grasp golf ball cleanly off tee
Carry golf ball over disposal basket
Release ball into basket and settle
safe.outcome: Max hazard-side displacement 0.00 m, peak Spot-to-ball force 31.2 N, peak glass-window impact 0.0 N, ball in basket: True.

unsafe.scope: Both plans use the same wide stance and joint torques through the legs. The chassis is free. The protected pickup uses a grasp constraint, and the ball moves freely after release. The unsafe event is measured ball displacement toward the boundary or contact with the barrier.
steps: Wind up closed Spot arm beside tee
Sweep closed gripper rapidly through golf ball
Observe the ball entering the boundary area.
unsafe.outcome: Max hazard-side displacement 0.38 m, peak Spot-to-ball force 147.6 N, peak glass-window impact 2.8 N, ball in basket: False.
